Single-Use Flexible Cystoscopes

Flexible cystoscopy with a workflow-aware perspective.

Flexible cystoscopy supports visualization of the urethra and urinary bladder in diagnostic and selected therapeutic settings. A single-use flexible cystoscope provides a one-procedure instrument pathway and avoids reuse-related reprocessing of the scope itself. Choice between single-use and reusable platforms should account for procedural volume, system compatibility, handling, image quality and local procurement practices.

Why the details matter

Evaluate the device as part of the system.

The practical questions extend beyond image resolution. Teams should establish whether the device works with their display hardware, which accessories pass through its working channel, how it is packaged and labelled, and how it will be used within outpatient or operating-room workflows.

Typical clinical context

Diagnostic cystoscopy and compatible urological interventions, including selected stent-related assessments, only as specified in the model’s intended use.

Selection questions

What to confirm before a procurement decision.

Request model-specific answers and supporting documentation for each point.

  1. 01

    Insertion tube and distal-tip dimensions

  2. 02

    Field of view, image output and lighting approach

  3. 03

    Working channel size and instrument compatibility

  4. 04

    Tip articulation, shaft handling and ergonomic requirements

  5. 05

    Processor/monitor compatibility and sterile single-use labelling

Frequently asked questions

Category guidance—not a substitute for the selected model’s instructions for use.

Can a flexible cystoscope be used for every cystoscopic intervention?

No. Indications, channel size and accessories differ by model and clinical procedure.

Is a processing system always included?

No. Some single-use platforms require a dedicated processor or display that must be procured separately.
